_comment: Operating parameters for the StockCare routing service. The backend sends only stops, priority coefficients and vehicles; every solver-tuning knob lives here so ops can retune without redeploying the JVM.

priorite._comment: The priority model is the single source of the coefficient; this service only rescales it. The Spring backend emits 0..100 (MockPriorityCalculationService), while the MILP objective and the SLA anchors below live in the catalogue's 0..1 domain (0.058..0.662). Set echelle_entree=1.0 if a future priority model already emits 0..1.

sla._comment: Deadline T[i] in minutes, interpolated from the aggregated priority coefficient. Higher priority => tighter window. Mirrors milp_care/config/config.json.

dechargement._comment: Service time sigma[i] in minutes: flat rate + increment per order line.

geometrie._comment: Distance-tiered speed/sinuosity so a single depot can reach pharmacies across Tunisia, not just its own city. The <15km tier is the real TomTom calibration (13 Sousse trips, 18/07/2026, sinuosity 1.6, 20.9km/h); it stays untouched for local/urban stops. Beyond that, a single national factor was wildly wrong (e.g. Tunis->Sfax haversine ~235km x1.6 / 20.9km/h => ~18h, vs H_max=480min => every stop past ~50km was structurally unroutable). Regional and highway tiers below are literature-typical Tunisian road averages (regional roads ~50-60km/h, autoroute/RN with town crossings ~80-90km/h), pending real calibration once build_matrix_from_tomtom (geometrie.py) or an OSRM instance is wired in.

_legacy_flat_fallback._comment: Kept only for tooling that still calls build_matrix_calibrated() directly with a flat factor (e.g. milp_care_delivery/scenarios.py, which only ever runs on a tight Sousse cluster).

flotte._comment: Vehicle capacities and refrigeration come from the backend. Only the per-km cost is set here, since the fleet table carries no cost column.
